title: Frontier-lab safety frameworks align on catastrophic-risk disclosure by Q2 2027
body: The Great American AI Act discussion draft conditions its three-year preemption of state development laws on a new federal disclosure: any frontier developer above roughly $500M in prior-year gross revenue must publish a public framework describing how it evaluates and manages a model's catastrophic risks. Several of the labs that clear that threshold already maintain their own catastrophic-risk safety frameworks under different names and structures, so the draft's mandatory-disclosure shape gives them a strong incentive to act before a bill is ever voted on. The prediction is that the largest frontier developers will voluntarily revise and re-publish their existing safety frameworks to converge on a common disclosure structure that mirrors the draft's framework requirement, treating the bill text as the template the industry standardizes around. Moving first lets the labs define what a compliant catastrophic-risk disclosure looks like, blunt the safety-advocate argument that a federal ceiling weakens the state-law floor, and lock in a uniform regime they can defend in lobbying as the draft moves toward formal introduction. Concretely, by the second quarter of 2027 at least three over-threshold developers will publish framework updates that explicitly track the federal disclosure shape, well ahead of any enacted statutory deadline.

reasoning.because: House draft would force >$500M frontier developers to publish a catastrophic-risk framework
reasoning.given: Top labs already run rival safety frameworks and want to shape the bill, not merely react to it
reasoning.so_that: Labs voluntarily converge their published frameworks toward the draft template to set the de facto standard pre-vote
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; >=3 over-threshold labs publish updates citing the federal shape
reasoning.plain_language: A draft law would make big AI firms publish how they guard against catastrophic risks, so they will agree on one shared format first.

summary: The Great American AI Act draft would require frontier developers above ~$500M in revenue to publish a catastrophic-risk framework. Rather than wait for a vote, the largest labs that already run safety frameworks will voluntarily align them on a shared template to set the standard a bill codifies.
